title: Adaptation and Evolution
seo_title: Year 6 Science: Adaptation and Evolution Worksheets (Darwin, Finches, Peppered Moths)
standard_text: Identify how animals and plants are adapted to suit their environment in different ways and that adaptation may lead to evolution.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 science worksheets on adaptation and evolution: animal and plant adaptations, natural selection, Darwin's finches, peppered moths and Alfred Russel Wallace. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Suited to survive, changed over time.
key_sub: Adaptations help survival; natural selection changes species over many generations.
body_html:
How to think about it

Living things are adapted to their environment, and over many generations they evolve.

  • Adaptations are inherited features, such as a polar bear's thick fat or a cactus's spines.
  • Natural selection: individuals vary; those best suited survive and breed; their useful features pass on; over many generations the species changes.
  • Darwin (finches) and Wallace worked this out. Peppered moths changed colour as Britain's air changed.
Example

A finch has a large, strong beak. Food?

Strong beaks crack hard things

Answer: hard seeds

Example

Trees go black with soot. Which moths survive?

Dark moths are hidden

Answer: dark moths

Common mistakes

  • Thinking an animal changes its body because it wants or needs to.
  • Thinking evolution happens in one lifetime.
  • Thinking soot turned the moths black.

faq.q: What is the difference between adaptation and evolution?
faq.a: An adaptation is an inherited feature that helps a living thing survive. Evolution is the slow change of a species over many generations, as useful adaptations become more common.
Individuals vary. Those best suited to their environment survive and breed, passing on their features. Over many generations, the species changes.

faq.q: What happened to the peppered moths?
faq.a: When soot blackened trees in industrial Britain, dark moths were better hidden from birds and became common. When the air was cleaned, pale moths became common again.
